scenes.heading: How Photosynthesis Works
scenes.text: Sunlight in. Food and oxygen out.
scenes.narration: Photosynthesis is how plants turn sunlight into food. Here is how it works.

scenes.heading: Three ingredients
scenes.narration: Every plant needs three ingredients: sunlight from above, water from the soil, and carbon dioxide from the air.

scenes.heading: Catching the light
scenes.text: Chlorophyll, the green pigment, absorbs sunlight.
scenes.narration: Leaves contain chlorophyll, a green pigment that captures light energy from the sun.

scenes.text: Of Earth's oxygen comes from ocean phytoplankton.
scenes.source: The ocean is the planet's largest forest
scenes.narration: Half of the oxygen in the atmosphere comes from tiny ocean plants called phytoplankton.

scenes.heading: What happens in a leaf
scenes.narration: Light energy splits water into hydrogen and oxygen. Carbon dioxide is then combined into glucose, and oxygen is released.

scenes.quote: Nearly every breath you take came from a leaf.
scenes.narration: Nearly every breath you take comes from a leaf, or from the ocean doing the same thing.

scenes.heading: Feeding the world
scenes.text: Crops, forests, and plankton anchor every food chain.
scenes.narration: Farms, forests, and ocean plankton all photosynthesize, forming the base of nearly every food chain.

scenes.heading: Reels
scenes.narration: That is photosynthesis. Sunlight in, life out.
